title: Calorespirometry: A Powerful, Noninvasive Approach to Investigate Cellular Energy Metabolism
protocol: Maintain human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's medium (DMEM).
Add 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 10 mM glucose, 2 mM glutamine, and 1 mM pyruvate to the DMEM.
Culture the cells at 37 °C in a cell culture incubator with 5% CO2 and 95% air.
Plate the cells at 1 x 10^6 cells per 100 mm culture plate.
Subculture the cells every 7 days or before reaching 90% confluency.
Renew the medium every 3 to 4 days.
Perform experiments when cells are 60 to 80% confluent.
Pipette 2.2 mL of DMEM into the respirometer chamber.
Insert the stopper fully and adjust it with the stopper spacer tool for optimal oxygen diffusion from air to medium.
Stir continuously at 37 °C until oxygen concentration (blue trace) and oxygen flux (red trace) are stable.
Calibrate the respirometer's software to account for the oxygen solubility of DMEM, which is 0.92.
Select a stable portion of the oxygen concentration trace after stabilization in DMEM with the chamber open.
Calibrate this stable portion for 100% air saturation.
Calibrate for 0% oxygen selecting a stable portion of the oxygen concentration trace when no oxygen is present in the chamber.
Perform this step after 20 µL titration of 230 mM sodium dithionite or after all oxygen is consumed by the biological sample at the end of an experiment.
After the 100% air calibration of the respirometer, close the stopper and ensure that no bubbles are present in the chamber.
Add 2.5 mL of H2O to the reference ampule of the calorimeter and tighten the cap using pliers if necessary.
Clean the sealed ampule with airflow and slowly lower the ampule to position 1 in the reference channel of the calorimeter.
Warm DMEM and trypsin to 37 °C in a water bath.
Add DMEM to a fresh 100-mm plate and place in the incubator to allow for equilibration.
Confirm cell confluence between 60 - 80% using an inverted light microscope.
Wash the 100-mm plate twice with 10 mL of room temperature phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Add 3 mL of 37-°C trypsin to the 100-mm plate and incubate for 7 - 10 min at 37 °C.
Neutralize the trypsin with 3 mL of 37-°C DMEM and suspend by gently pipetting it ~20 times.
Transfer the resuspended cells into a sterile 15-mL conical tube and centrifuge for 5 min at 175 x g.
Remove the liquid without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ~5 mL of DMEM and mix thoroughly to dissociate the cells from one another.
Remove ~100 μL of the well-mixed sample and perform a thorough cell count utilizing all 8 fields on a hemocytometer.
Calculate the volume for resuspension of the cells to generate ~2 x 10^6 cells per 50 μL.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 175 x g.
Resuspend the pellet in the calculated volume of DMEM.
Perform a cell count to determine the volume required to inject 2 x 10^6 cells per chamber in the respirometer.
Store the cells for the respirometric measurement on ice until ready.
Determine the dilution required to produce a concentration of 1 x 10^5 cells/mL for calorimetry while the concentrated cell sample is on ice.
Mix the sample well and prepare approximately 3 mL of cells at 1 x 10^5 cells/mL in DMEM for each ampule.
Ensure that the calorimeter is connected to the computer and the calorimetric signal in µW is observable and stable.
Add 2.5 mL of cells at 1 x 10^5 cells/mL (~2.5 x 10^5 cells) to each ampule, ensuring sufficient air for gas diffusion between the lid of the ampule and the medium.
Tighten the cap immediately, using pliers if necessary.
Clean the sealed ampule, using airflow to remove any external debris.
Slowly lower the ampule to position 1 of the calorimeter.
Record the time the ampule is lowered to position 1.
Allow the ampule to sit at position 1 for 15 minutes.
After 15 min at position 1, slowly lower both the reference and sample ampules to position 2.
Record the time the ampules were lowered.
Measure for at least 30 min.
Thoroughly mix the cell sample by pipetting.
Inject less than 50 µL of the cell sample into each chamber of the respirometer.
Ensure a final concentration of approximately 2 x 10^6 cells per chamber.
Record the time the cells are injected into the respirometer.
Wait at least 20 - 30 min for both a stabilization of the oxygen flux and a steady decrease in the oxygen concentration.
Select the O2 flux per V tab on the right of the screen.
Highlight a stable portion of oxygen flux.
Select marks, then statistics and record data for O2 flux per V.
Inject 1 µL of 4mg/mL oligomycin into each chamber.
Allow approximately 10 min for oxygen flux stabilization after adding oligomycin.
Record stable leak respiration rate by following steps performed in highlighting a stable portion of the oxygen flux trace.
Titrate 2-µL injections of 0.2 mM FCCP into each chamber.
Allow oxygen flux stabilization after each injection.
Continue titrations until the maximal flux is reached, as indicated by a slight decline in subsequent FCCP titration.
Record the stable respiration rate during the maximal flux.
Perform a final cell count utilizing all 8 fields of a hemocytometer to determine the total number of cells added to the ampule.
Determine a time to record measurements from both calorimeter and respirometer when stable signals are present at identical times.
Reference the time recorded when the ampule was lowered to position 2.
Record the heat production by placing the cursor over the trace displaying heat output for the respective ampule at the determined time, expressing as µW/million cells.
Collect oxygen consumption data and ensure it is expressed as pmol O2 x s-1 x million cells.
